tables.heading_context: ## Select JNI, FFM, or a Process
rows: Broad JDK compatibility; existing native methods
Verbose handles, local/global refs, classloader/thread rules
Controlled modern JDK baseline; C-shaped native library
JDK-version policy and newer ecosystem tooling
Lower-volume calls and faster wrapper development
Dynamic mapping overhead and less compile-time checking
Strong failure, heap, and rollout isolation
Return status/result data, then throw a documented Java exception
Catch/map to terminal native failure; never unwind into JVM
Run on a Java executor or native worker; do not block sensitive JVM threads
Complete `CompletableFuture` through an attached JVM thread
Explicit cancel handle/flag; define whether work stops or result is ignored
JNI/system ABI or FFM-to-C ABI only; never expose Rust ABI, `repr(Rust)`, or trait objects.
JVM owns Java objects; Rust frees Rust handles/buffers; FFM arenas do not free arbitrary Rust allocations.
Catch/map Rust panic; Java exceptions remain pending/handled through JVM APIs and never unwind through Rust.
Local/global JNI refs, array pins, `MemorySegment` scopes, and opaque handles each need explicit duration.
`JNIEnv` is thread-affine; attach workers, define callback executor/reentrancy, and respect GC-sensitive regions.
Test JDK range, JNI/FFM adapter, OS, architecture, libc, and JVM distribution constraints.
Ship/select/extract native libraries securely; include dependencies, symbols, signing, and classloader behavior.
Runtime adapter over a C-shaped Rust operation
Explicit off-heap view with lifetime and position/limit semantics
Managed owner of an opaque Rust handle
Completion projected from native work on a JVM-safe path
Java projection over functions/handles, not a Rust trait-object vtable
Controlled JDK 22+ estate and C-shaped API
Direct buffer/segment with explicit lifetime, or copy
Attach thread, use global refs, marshal to chosen executor
Platform artifacts plus clean JVM load tests
